note: Every number was counted by the command written next to it, inside the project folder. Left out of every count: node_modules, hidden folders, data/, portfolio/, coverage/ and *.d.ts files.

project.name: neighbor-node
project.type: Web app: one Next.js project that holds the pages, the server actions and the storage, plus a small command-line tool for the person who runs the site.
project.problem: Neighbors need a simple place to ask for help, offer help and lend things, without accounts and without showing an exact address.
project.who_uses_it: People who live near each other (from README.md).

features.text: Read the board of posts and filter it by kind (Help wanted, Offer, Lend)
Write a post; the server checks it again before it saves it to one JSON file
No accounts: each post gets a secret key, and only a SHA-256 fingerprint of it is saved
A private page for the author: edit the post, change its status, read replies, see report counts, take it down
A post nobody touches for 30 days is hidden from the board, never deleted; the author can keep it up
Neighbors reply privately; only the author reads the replies
Visitors report a post with a reason, never a name
Speed limits on every public action, counted in the memory of the running server
A command-line tool that lists reports and takes posts down, with a backup first
Light and dark theme from CSS variables
Safe headers on every page, and no X-Powered-By header
A share image that is drawn when the site is built
robots.txt and a sitemap that leaves out every post

files_code.command: sum of: files_ts files_tsx files_mts files_mjs

lines_code.what: Lines of code (.ts, .tsx, .mts, .mjs), blank lines and comments included
lines_code.command: sum of: lines_ts lines_tsx lines_mts lines_mjs

error_pages.what: Error and not-found pages in app/

route_handlers.what: API route handlers (route.ts files in app/)

server_action_files.what: Files in app/ that are server actions

server_actions.what: Server actions (exported async functions in the files that are server actions)
server_actions.command: grep -rl '"use server"' app | while read -r f; do grep -h '^export async function' "$f"; done | wc -l

database_files.command: find . \( -type d \( -name '.?*' -o -name node_modules -o -name data -o -name portfolio -o -name coverage \) -prune \) -o -type f \( -name '*.sql' -o -name 'schema.prisma' -o -name '*.db' -o -name '*.sqlite' \) -print | wc -l

limit_rule_files.what: Speed-limit rule files in lib/ (*-limits.ts, without live-*)

aria_attributes.what: aria-* attributes written in app/ and components/

post_kinds.command: awk '/export const postKindIds/ { go = 1 } go { print } go && /as const/ { exit }' lib/post-kinds.ts | grep -o '"[a-z-]*"' | wc -l

post_statuses.command: awk '/export const postStatusIds/ { go = 1 } go { print } go && /as const/ { exit }' lib/posts.ts | grep -o '"[a-z-]*"' | wc -l

report_reasons.command: awk '/export const reportReasonIds/ { go = 1 } go { print } go && /as const/ { exit }' lib/report-reasons.ts | grep -o '"[a-z-]*"' | wc -l

hide_after_days.what: Days after which a post that nobody touched is hidden

post_limit_per_visitor.what: Posts one visitor may save in an hour

post_limit_per_site.what: Posts the whole site accepts in an hour

manage_wrong_tries.what: Wrong tries on a private page, for one visitor

manage_window_minutes.what: Minutes a wrong try on a private page counts

replies_per_hour.what: Replies one visitor may send in an hour

test_files_logic.what: Test files for rules and storage (*.test.ts)

test_files_components.what: Test files for pages and components (*.test.tsx)

test_definitions.what: Tests written (lines that start a test or it call in __tests__/)

special_files.what: Files in app/ that make robots.txt, the sitemap and the share image

server_action_list.what: Server actions (exported async functions in the files that are server actions)
server_action_list.command: grep -rl '"use server"' app | while read -r f; do grep -hoE '^export async function [A-Za-z]+' "$f"; done | sed 's/^export async function //' | sort

quick_start.what: Quick start commands, as written in README.md
quick_start.command: sed -n '/^## Quick start/,/^| Command/p' README.md | grep '^    ' | sed 's/^    //'

dev_address.what: Address of the site in development, as written in README.md

setting_names.what: Settings the server reads, as listed in README.md (names only)
